_provenance: SOURCE-DERIVED, NOT LIVE. Built from codex-rs @ rust-v0.167.0: core/src/tools/approvals.rs ApprovalAction::permission_request_payload (NetworkAccess arm -> PermissionRequestPayload::bash), core/src/tools/network_approval.rs (hook_command, format_network_target, prompt_reason), app-server PR #58350 (NetworkApprovalResolved -> outgoing.resolve_server_request -> serverRequest/resolved). A live attempt on macOS with [features.network_proxy] did not trigger the managed proxy (upstream network-approval tests are Linux-only). Angle-bracket values are placeholders.
_hook_notes: tool_input.command is the TRIGGERING shell command when an owning exec call exists, else the literal 'network-access <protocol>://<host>:<port>'. tool_input.description is always 'network-access <protocol>://<host>:<port>'. tool_name is 'Bash' (indistinguishable by name from a command approval; the description prefix is the only marker). If the request ends while the hook is still running, the approval future is dropped and the hook's process group gets SIGKILL (hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs ProcessTreeGuard -> utils/pty kill_process_group). No hook output, no event to the hook.

params.reason: Network access to example.com requires approval

messages._note: Emitted with NO client reply when Codex withdraws the prompt (request ended / execution gone / thread shutdown). The pending JSON-RPC request is also cancelled. Only happens if the terminal/app-server prompt was already open, i.e. the PermissionRequest hook had returned without a decision.

_rollout_notes: Nothing persisted: EventMsg::NetworkApprovalResolved is listed as non-persisted in rollout/src/policy.rs (PR #58350), and exec approval requests are not persisted either. The rollout only shows the eventual tool output.
